A tube that lights in your hand. 'Teach what they tried to hide' doesn't mean 'believe what you're told' — it means giving you the tools to see for yourself. Every lesson in this app should end the same way: with something you can DO.

Experiment 8: the 7-day mental prototype challenge

Tesla's REAL superpower wasn't electricity — it was the mental prototyping from the Workshop lesson (Project 7). This week, train it deliberately. Pick ONE small problem in your life (a cluttered room, a slow morning routine, a wobbly shelf). DAYS 1–3: build the solution in your mind for 10 minutes nightly — see every step, every object, in 3D. DAYS 4–5: run the mental model and watch it FAIL — where does it break? Fix that part. DAYS 6–7: build it physically. WHAT YOU'LL FIND: the physical build goes shockingly smoothly, because you already failed in your head. Tesla claimed he never needed prototypes because his mental models never failed — yours will fail at first, and that's the training. Journal each night: what broke in the model, what you changed. That's the method.

Experiment 9: the Tesla scavenger hunt (your home)

Walk through your home and find FIVE Tesla inventions hiding in plain sight. (1) Anything with a motor — fridge, fan, washing machine (his induction motor). (2) The breaker panel's 240V double breaker (his polyphase system). (3) Any remote control (his teleautomaton). (4) A phone charger, especially wireless (his resonance). (5) Any radio — car, alarm clock (his tuned circuits, vindicated 1943). Touch each one and say what it is. WHAT THIS TEACHES: Tesla isn't history — he's infrastructure. The 'hidden genius' isn't hidden at all; he's just so successful he became invisible. Beginners who do this scavenger hunt never read the Tesla lessons the same way again.

Experiment 10: prosecute and defend Edison

Argue BOTH sides, out loud or on paper, 10 minutes each. SIDE A (prosecution): Edison was a ruthless businessman who electrocuted animals to smear AC, underpaid Tesla, and took credit for his lab's work. SIDE B (defense): Edison built the first real R&D lab, gave Tesla his start, electrified cities with DC where it worked, and his 'theft' is mostly meme. Then render a VERDICT with evidence citations (patent numbers, dates). WHY: the teaching's hero/villain stories are useful but dangerous — this exercise forces you past team colors into evidence. You'll end up respecting both men and trusting neither myth. That's the verification mindset, weaponized.

Experiment 11: audit your own threes (one week)

For one week, carry a pocket notebook and log EVERY time you catch yourself doing something in threes — or wanting to. Checking the lock twice-then-once-more. Three sips before setting the cup down. The third glance at the phone. Don't judge it; just tally. At week's end, count the marks. WHAT YOU'LL LEARN: ritualized repetition is already running in your nervous system — Tesla's documented compulsion is an extreme version of something every human does. The honest question the Living 3-6-9 lesson raises: are your threes serving you (calming rhythm) or ruling you (anxiety loop)? If a pattern causes DISTRESS or eats your time, that's worth discussing with a professional — ritual is a tool; compulsion is a cage. Know which one you're holding.

Experiment 12: teach one experiment to someone else

Pick ONE experiment from this lesson — the doubling proof is perfect — and teach it to someone else this week: a friend, a kid, a parent. No notes; explain it from memory, on paper, while they watch. WHAT HAPPENS: the parts you stumble on are the parts you don't actually understand yet — go back, re-learn them, teach again. Physicists call this the Feynman technique; it's the fastest known way to convert 'I read it' into 'I know it.' Tesla's ideas survived because he could DEMONSTRATE them — the boat, the coil, the egg. Knowledge you can't demonstrate is trivia. Knowledge you can teach is yours.

The builder's oath

Twelve experiments, one oath. Say it out loud: 'I will not believe — I will verify. I will check the patent, run the math, build the thing, journal the result. I will separate the legend from the record, even when the legend is prettier. And I will teach what I verify to someone else.' That's the entire Tesla section in one paragraph — and honestly, it's the entire APP in one paragraph. 'Teach what they tried to hide' was never about memorizing hidden facts. It's about becoming the kind of person who can't BE fooled — because you check. Go build.

Read 'My Inventions' free (it's public domain)

Tesla's 1919 autobiography — six magazine installments, now public domain and free everywhere (Project Gutenberg and others). Read it in one sitting: it's short, strange, and completely his voice — the visions, the compulsions, the engineering, the grief. No biographer, no meme page, no app lesson substitutes for the man's own account. Assignment: read it, then re-read the tesla-life lesson and notice what the memes added. That's your calibration exercise for every Tesla claim you'll ever meet.

The 60 Hz hum hunt (safe, real, tonight)

Tesla's world runs at 60 cycles per second (North America) — and you can HEAR it. Tonight: hold your phone near anything plugged in and open a free spectrum-analyzer app; you'll see the 60 Hz spike. Old transformers audibly hum at 60 Hz (120 Hz harmonic too). That's the polyphase grid — Tesla's system — singing. It was 60 Hz because Tesla and Westinghouse picked it; Europe picked 50. You're hearing a 130-year-old engineering decision. That's not mysticism — it's infrastructure you can measure.

The compass and the rotating field (safe, 5 minutes)

Tesla's core insight, on your desk: put a compass on the table, bring a bar magnet near, and rotate the magnet — the needle follows, rotating without touching. That's the rotating magnetic field in miniature: a turning magnet drags another magnet around with it. Tesla's leap was doing it with ELECTROMAGNETS switched in sequence — no moving parts, just timed pulses creating a phantom rotation that drags the rotor. The compass demo is the whole motor, shrunk. Show a kid; watch the exact moment they get it.

Prosecute AND defend Edison (the thinking exercise)

Two columns, pen and paper. PROSECUTE: the elephant electrocutions (documented — Edison's people electrocuted animals to smear AC), the smear campaign, taking credit. DEFEND: he built the first real R&D lab, electrified cities first, gave Tesla his start, and DC is actually better for short distances and electronics (your phone charges on DC). The exercise isn't about picking a winner — it's about holding a whole human. History's villains are usually just competitors who won the ugly parts.

The Wardenclyffe pilgrimage (plan it)

The Tesla Science Center at Wardenclyffe (Shoreham, Long Island) — the actual site, with Tesla's lab building still standing. The Nikola Tesla Museum in Belgrade holds his ashes, his papers, and working models of his inventions. You don't need to worship; you need to STAND where it happened. The tower's foundations are still in the ground. Bring the honest version of the story with you — it makes the place more powerful, not less.

Teach the doubling proof to a skeptic (the final exam)

Find the most skeptical person you know and walk them through the doubling circuit on paper — 1, 2, 4, 8, 7, 5, 1 — then the tripling proof that always lands on 9. Then say the honest sentence: 'The math is real, the quote is unsourced, and Tesla never taught this.' If you can hold someone's wonder AND their skepticism in the same conversation, you've learned the thing this whole section is trying to teach: honesty doesn't kill magic — it protects it.

Experiment 0: the pre-lab (do this first)

Before the twelve experiments — the setup that makes them work. THE LAB NOTEBOOK (see Workshop Project 12): one bound notebook, dated entries, EVERY experiment logged — hypothesis, method, observation, conclusion. Tesla’s notebooks were his real laboratory; yours will be too. THE MINDSET CONTRACT: write this on page 1 — ‘I will record what HAPPENS, not what I hoped. Failed experiments are data.’ THE BASELINE WEEK: before experimenting, journal one normal week — sleep, energy, mood, 1–10 daily. Every later experiment gets compared to THIS. THE TEACHING’S POINT: the experiments are worthless without the notebook — memory edits, paper doesn’t. The pre-lab takes one week and multiplies every later experiment’s value by ten.

Experiment 13: the Faraday cage test (your phone)

Tesla’s world was fields — test your own. THE EXPERIMENT: wrap your phone COMPLETELY in aluminum foil (3–4 layers, no gaps) — then call it from another phone. WHAT HAPPENS: it won’t ring — the foil is a FARADAY CAGE, blocking the radio frequencies (ESTABLISHED physics, 1836). UNWRAP one corner — it rings. THE LESSON: electromagnetic fields are BLOCKABLE by conductors — which is why the ‘scalar waves pass through everything’ claim (see that lesson) needs extraordinary evidence: ordinary EM does NOT pass through everything. VARIATIONS: try the microwave (don’t turn it on) — same principle, engineered. THE TEACHING’S USE: this 5-minute test gives you a FEEL for fields that no lecture provides — and a bullshit-detector for field claims. Tesla would approve: verify with foil.

Experiment 14: the compass and the wire (Oersted, 1820)

The experiment that started electromagnetism — repeat it. YOU NEED: a compass, a battery, a length of wire. THE METHOD: lay the wire over the compass needle (aligned north-south), connect the battery briefly — the needle JUMPS sideways. Disconnect — it returns. WHAT YOU’VE PROVEN: electric current creates a MAGNETIC field (Oersted’s 1820 discovery — DOCUMENTED, the founding moment of electromagnetism). REVERSE IT: move a magnet near the wire, watch a meter (or a second compass) — motion creates current (Faraday). THESE TWO — current↔magnetism, both directions — are the entire foundation Tesla built on. THE TEACHING’S POINT: every ‘impossible’ Tesla claim rests on these two humble facts. Do the experiment and you are standing where the whole electrical age started — compass in hand.

Experiment 15: the 30-day verification journal

The meta-experiment — testing the TESTING. THE METHOD: for 30 days, run one small verification daily — not all Tesla: verify a news claim (check the source), a health claim (find the study), a spiritual claim (test the practice). LOG EACH: claim, source checked, verdict (confirmed/debunked/unresolved). THE PATTERN you’ll find: roughly a third of confident claims collapse on contact with primary sources — the ‘everyone knows’ files are the thinnest. THE TEACHING’S PAYOFF: after 30 days you will have a calibrated bullshit-detector — and you will trust the surviving claims (including this app’s) MORE, because you tested them. The verification mindset (Step 8) is not cynicism — it is the highest form of respect for truth. The journal is the instrument; you are the experiment.

Teaching Tesla to kids: the 5 experiments that land

The builder’s oath (Step 13) says teach — here is the kid-tested set. (1) THE BALLOON STATIC: rub a balloon, stick it to the wall, pick up paper bits — electrostatics at age 5. (2) THE COMPASS WIRE (previous step) — the needle jump delights every age. (3) THE DOUBLING PROOF (Experiment 1) — kids love the 1-2-4-8-7-5 loop; make it a race. (4) THE FOIL PHONE (previous step) — ‘the invisible shield’ is pure magic to a 10-year-old. (5) THE LEMON BATTERY: lemon + copper penny + zinc nail = measurable voltage (a voltmeter makes it real) — electrochemistry from fruit. THE TEACHING’S RULE: never explain first — let them SEE it, then ask ‘why do you think that happened?’ The question is the teaching; the experiment is just the hook. Tesla’s legacy is not the tower — it is the next kid who refuses to stop asking.

🛠️ The Tesla Workshop: How to Do Every One

Every Tesla topic, picked apart into HOW: what you need, how to put it together, why it works, and how you'll know it worked. The build-it lesson.

Project 1: the Egg of Columbus (Tesla's own demo)

WHAT: Tesla's favorite party trick — a copper egg that stands on end and spins when placed in a rotating magnetic field. It was his proof-of-concept for the induction motor. HOW TO DO IT: you need 4 coils of magnet wire, an iron core frame (or 3D-printed holder), and a two-phase AC source — a low-voltage AC transformer with a phase-splitter circuit (plans are all over maker forums; search 'Egg of Columbus DIY'). Place a hollow copper egg (or copper-coated egg shape) in the center and power up. WHY IT WORKS: the rotating field induces currents in the egg; the currents make their own field; the fields chase each other and the egg spins upright. VERIFY: the egg rises and spins with nothing touching it. You just replicated 1888.

Project 2: wind your own Tesla coil secondary

WHAT: the heart of every Tesla coil is the tall secondary coil — hundreds of turns of fine wire. Winding it yourself teaches resonance physically. YOU NEED: a PVC pipe (2–3 inch diameter, ~10 inches long), ~500 feet of thin magnet wire (28–30 AWG), patience. HOW: anchor the wire at the bottom, wind tightly turn-by-turn upward — no overlaps, no gaps — for several evenings. This IS the meditation: Tesla wound his own. WHY IT WORKS: the tall coil has a natural resonant frequency; the primary circuit pumps energy at that frequency and voltage multiplies enormously. VERIFY: with a simple driver circuit (a 'slayer exciter' — the beginner's solid-state driver, plans online), your hand-wound coil throws real sparks. You built the lightning box.

Project 3: the CD turbine (Tesla's bladeless turbine, desktop edition)

WHAT: Tesla's 1913 bladeless turbine, shrunk to your desk. YOU NEED: 5–6 old CDs (the discs), a bolt/axle through their centers with small spacers between them, two plates to sandwich the stack, and a nozzle — an air compressor, or even a balloon with a straw. HOW: mount the CD stack on the axle so it spins freely; aim the air jet at the EDGE of the discs, tangent to the stack. WHY IT WORKS: the boundary layer — air drags on the smooth disc surfaces and the whole stack spins with no blades at all. VERIFY: it spins fast on air alone. Tesla's 'greatest achievement,' running on a balloon.

Project 4: catch the sky (the radiant energy experiment)

WHAT: Tesla's atmospheric energy idea, made measurable. YOU NEED: a long wire antenna (30+ feet, as high as you can get it), a good ground rod, and a sensitive voltmeter or electroscope. HOW: connect the antenna through a diode to the meter, ground the other side. WHY IT WORKS: the Earth and ionosphere hold a real voltage difference (hundreds of thousands of volts across the sky); your wire samples a tiny slice of it. VERIFY: the meter reads a real, persistent voltage — free energy from the sky, measured. The honest half: it's microwatts, not house-power. You proved the physics AND its limits in one afternoon.

Project 5: read your home like Tesla (the polyphase walkthrough)

WHAT: find Tesla's system alive in your walls. YOU NEED: your breaker panel and 10 minutes. HOW: open the panel (don't touch wires) — find the big double breaker labeled for the dryer or stove. That's 240V: TWO hot legs, each 120V, opposite in phase — split-phase, the domestic descendant of Tesla's polyphase. Trace which rooms are on which leg. WHY IT WORKS: the two legs are 180 degrees apart, so leg-to-leg gives 240V for heavy loads while leg-to-neutral gives 120V for everything else. VERIFY: every heavy appliance in your home runs on Tesla's phase trick. You've been living inside his invention your whole life.

Project 6: send your first wireless signal (the teleautomaton spirit)

WHAT: Tesla's 1898 remote-control boat, beginner edition. YOU NEED: a cheap 433MHz transmitter/receiver pair (a few dollars online) and an Arduino or similar board — or a pre-made remote relay kit, no coding needed. HOW: wire the receiver to a relay controlling an LED or small motor; press the transmitter button across the room. WHY IT WORKS: the transmitter encodes a radio pulse; the receiver decodes it — the exact principle of the Madison Square Garden boat, miniaturized. VERIFY: the light obeys your hand from across the room with no wire. In 1898, crowds called this telepathy.

Project 7: think like Tesla (his actual mental method)

WHAT: Tesla's visualization — his true superpower, and the one project needing zero parts. YOU NEED: quiet and 15 minutes. HOW: pick a simple machine (a bicycle, a fan). Close your eyes and BUILD it in your mind — every part, in 3D, rotating. Run it. Watch it for imagined 'weeks': which part wears first? Change that part. Run it again. This is exactly what Tesla described doing — mental prototyping until the design stopped failing. WHY IT WORKS: the brain's spatial simulator is powerful; engineers call it mental modeling, athletes call it visualization. VERIFY: after a week of practice, your mental models get sharper and more stable. You're training the faculty Tesla was born with.

Project 8: the safety chapter (read before touching voltage)

Tesla survived his experiments; you must too. RULES: (1) Never work on anything plugged into wall power while building — batteries and low-voltage supplies only, until you know exactly what you're doing. (2) High voltage can burn and stop hearts — treat every coil as live. (3) One hand behind your back near high voltage (keeps current from crossing your chest). (4) Pacemakers, electronics, and curious pets stay far away. (5) Kids build WITH an adult, always. The teaching honors Tesla best by keeping his students alive.

The workshop mindset

Notice what just happened: every 'impossible genius' idea became a weekend project, a wire, a CD, a meter reading. That's the method — pick it apart until it's parts, put the parts together, watch it work. Tesla wasn't magic; he was methodical. 'Teaching what they tried to hide' was never about worshipping him — it's about becoming the kind of person who builds.

Project 9: the crystal radio (Tesla's tuned circuits)

WHAT: the simplest radio on Earth — no battery, no plug, powered by the radio waves themselves. It uses exactly Tesla's tuned-circuit principles (the ones behind his radio patents). YOU NEED: a long wire antenna, a ground connection, a germanium diode (pennies online), a coil of magnet wire wound on a tube, and an old high-impedance earphone. HOW: antenna → coil → diode → earphone → ground; slide a tap along the coil to tune. WHY IT WORKS: the coil + antenna resonate at one station's frequency (Tesla's resonance); the diode rectifies the signal into audio; the station's own broadcast power drives the earphone. VERIFY: at night, you'll hear a real AM station in the earphone — music from thin air, no battery. Tesla's 1890s circuits, still working.

Project 10: the earth battery

WHAT: a battery made of dirt — the tiniest echo of Tesla's dream of drawing energy from the Earth itself. YOU NEED: two different metals (a copper pipe and a galvanized nail work), damp soil, and a multimeter. HOW: push both metals into the same patch of damp earth a few inches apart; connect the multimeter. WHY IT WORKS: dissimilar metals in an electrolyte (damp soil) form a galvanic cell — basic chemistry, established since Volta. VERIFY: the meter reads a fraction of a volt — real power from dirt. The honest half: it's microwatts, enough to prove the principle and nothing more — exactly like the 'catch the sky' experiment. Tesla dreamed of scaling this to the planet; you just proved why scaling is the whole problem.

Project 11: see the rotating field (compass demo)

WHAT: SEE the rotating magnetic field instead of taking it on faith. YOU NEED: 3–4 small coils of magnet wire arranged in a circle on a board, a low-voltage AC source with a phase splitter (or a 3-phase hobby driver board), and a compass in the center. HOW: power the coils; watch the compass needle. WHY IT WORKS: the phased coils create Tesla's rotating field; the needle chases it and spins — the invisible made visible. VERIFY: the needle rotates smoothly with nothing touching it. This is the 1888 Budapest-park vision on your desk — the moment AC beat DC, replayed in miniature. If you build only one visualization project, build this one.

Project 12: the lab notebook (his real method)

WHAT: Tesla's notebooks were legendary — detailed, dated, obsessive. Copy the method. YOU NEED: one bound notebook (not loose paper), a pen, and discipline. HOW: date every entry. Sketch BEFORE you build. Write what you EXPECT to happen (your hypothesis), then what ACTUALLY happened, then why they differ. Number your experiments. Tape in dead components with notes ('burned at 12V — why?'). WHY IT WORKS: the notebook turns tinkering into research — patterns emerge across weeks that single builds hide. VERIFY: after a month, you'll have a personal engineering text — and you'll catch your own mistakes faster. Tesla's memory was photographic; yours doesn't need to be — that's what the notebook is for.

Where to take it next (leveling up)

Done with the starter projects? Level up deliberately. NEXT STEPS: (1) Join a maker community — local hackerspaces/makerspaces have high-voltage mentors, oscilloscopes, and people who've already burned the components you're about to burn. (2) Forums: the Tesla coil mailing list and maker forums hold decades of hard-won safety and tuning knowledge — lurk, read the safety threads FIRST. (3) Kits: graduate from slayer exciters to proper dual-resonant solid-state coils (DRSSTC kits) — real engineering, real sparks. (4) Read Tesla's Colorado Springs Notes (published) — his actual lab diary, measurements and all. The workshop never ends; it just gets higher voltage. Bring the safety chapter with you.

The failure log (his real secret)

Tesla's notebooks are full of failures — coils that wouldn't resonate, turbines that warped, the tower that never transmitted. He kept going because each failure was DATA. Adopt the rule: every failed build gets a notebook entry titled 'what it taught me' — no entry, no lesson. Common beginner failures and their lessons: coil won't spark → usually tuning (primary/secondary frequency mismatch) — you just learned resonance the hard way. Motor won't spin → check phase order — you just learned polyphase. Burned component → you just learned respect for current. The teaching's final workshop truth: Tesla wasn't the man who never failed. He was the man who wrote down every failure and built again.

Project: the earth battery (safe, real voltage)

Bury a copper pipe and a zinc (galvanized) pipe a few feet apart in damp soil, connect a voltmeter — you'll read real voltage, often 0.5–1V. It's a galvanic cell using the earth as electrolyte: documented 19th-century tech (telegraphs used earth batteries). Scale it: more pairs in series, more volts. It won't run your house — the current is tiny — but it lights the honest question Tesla asked: the ground is ELECTRICALLY ALIVE, a vast conductor. Measure it yourself. That's worth more than a hundred free-energy videos.

Project: the crystal radio (Tesla's tuned circuits, no battery)

Build the classic crystal radio — coil, diode, earphone, long antenna wire. It pulls AM stations from the air with NO power source: the signal's own energy drives the earphone. This is Tesla's tuned-circuit principle made audible — resonance selecting one frequency from the storm. Kits cost little; the plans are public domain. When you hear a voice from nothing but wire and air, you'll understand why 1890s audiences thought Tesla was a magician. He wasn't. He was just tuned.

Project: measure resonance with two tuning forks (the principle, pure)

Strike one tuning fork, hold it near an identical silent one — the silent one starts humming. That's resonance: matched frequencies sharing energy through air. Now you understand the Tesla coil's secondary, the wireless lamp trick, and half of Wardenclyffe's theory in one hum. Tesla's whole wireless dream was tuning forks at planetary scale. The principle is proven on your desk; the scale-up is where honesty lives. Both lessons in one experiment.

Project: the lemon-battery array (the honest 'free energy')

Chain lemons (or potatoes) with copper and zinc electrodes until you can light an LED — usually 4–6 fruits. It works, it's chemistry not magic, and it teaches the real lesson: energy is everywhere in tiny amounts; the engineering problem is CONCENTRATING it usefully. Every 'free energy' device that actually works is one of these — real physics, tiny power. The devices that claim house-scale power from nothing are the ones that never survive a voltmeter. Build the lemon array, then apply its lesson to every claim you meet.

Project: map your home's electromagnetic fields (the invisible architecture)

Borrow or buy a cheap EMF meter (or use a phone app, less accurate but instructive). Walk your home: the panel hums, the microwave leaks, the bedroom is quiet(er). Map it on paper. You're seeing Tesla's world — the polyphase grid made visible as fields. The honest use: find where you sleep relative to the fields and decide for yourself what matters. The teaching's claim about 'dirty electricity' gets labels here — some concerns are documented (high-voltage lines and health: studied, mixed), most household fears are speculative. Measure first, conclude second.

The failure log: Tesla's real secret (his method, DOCUMENTED)

From 'My Inventions' and the biographies: Tesla ran THOUSANDS of mental simulations before building — but he also built, tested, watched fail, and adjusted. The Colorado Springs notes (published as the 'Colorado Springs Notes' — real, buyable) are full of measurements that didn't do what he hoped. His secret wasn't never failing; it was failing CHEAP (in his head first) and writing down every failure. Start your log tonight: date, what you tried, what happened, what you'll change. That's the entire Tesla method in one habit.

Project 0: the workspace (before you build)

Before Project 1 — the shop itself. THE SPACE: a table you can leave messy, good light, ventilation (soldering fumes are real). THE CORE KIT ($50–100 total): soldering iron + solder, wire strippers, needle-nose pliers, a digital multimeter (the single most important tool — $15, measures everything), helping-hands holder, safety glasses. THE RULES: (1) NEVER work tired — mistakes with electricity are unforgiving. (2) One hand in pocket when probing live circuits (the old electrician’s rule — keeps current from crossing the chest). (3) Unplug before rewiring — every time, no exceptions. THE TEACHING’S POINT: Tesla’s lab was not magic — it was ORGANIZED. The workshop chapter of his life began with a bench, not a breakthrough. Build the bench first.

Project 13: the AM radio from scratch (the full build)

Project 9’s crystal radio, expanded to a full build guide. YOU NEED: a germanium diode (1N34A — $2), 50 feet of magnet wire, a toilet-paper tube (the coil form), a variable capacitor (365pF — salvaged or $10), high-impedance earphone (crystal earpiece), an antenna wire (30+ feet, as high as possible), a ground (cold water pipe). THE BUILD: (1) Wind 60–80 turns of magnet wire on the tube — neat, tight, no overlaps. (2) Connect: antenna → coil → diode → earphone → ground. (3) The variable capacitor across the coil tunes stations. WHAT YOU’LL HEAR: faint AM stations — powered by NOTHING but the radio waves themselves. THE LESSON: Tesla’s tuned circuits (Step 5 of the Research lesson) are not theory — they are a toilet-paper tube that sings. Build it and the whole wireless age stops being abstract.

Project 14: the electric pendulum (resonance, visible)

Resonance is Tesla’s master concept — SEE it. YOU NEED: a string, a weight (a nut or bolt), a metronome app. THE BUILD: hang the pendulum, measure its natural period (time 10 swings, divide). THE EXPERIMENT: push it gently at RANDOM intervals — chaotic, small motion. Now push at EXACTLY its natural period (the metronome helps) — the swings grow HUGE with tiny pushes. THAT is resonance: small inputs, perfectly timed, building enormous response. THE TESLA CONNECTION: his coils are electrical pendulums — the primary ‘pushes’ the secondary at its natural frequency, and the voltage swings grow enormous. THE TEACHING’S METAPHOR: the spiritual practices work the same way — small daily inputs, at the natural rhythm, building over time. Resonance is not just physics; it is the app’s whole method.

Sourcing parts: the treasure map

The projects need parts — here is where builders actually get them. NEW: electronics suppliers (Digi-Key, Mouser — the real thing, fast shipping), Amazon/eBay (fine for kits, verify sellers for components). SURPLUS: local electronics surplus stores (every major city has one — the treasure caves of the builder world), ham radio swap meets. SALVAGE: old microwaves (transformers — DANGEROUS, see safety), CRT TVs (flyback transformers — DANGEROUS), printers (motors, rods — SAFE and superb). THE TEACHING’S RULE: salvage teaches more than buying — taking apart a printer teaches mechanisms no kit can. But the safety chapter (Project 8) is the price of admission: capacitors hold charge AFTER unplugging (discharge with a resistor, never a screwdriver across the terminals — the old-timers’ missing fingertips are the warning).

The showcase: documenting and sharing your builds

Tesla’s notebooks were for HIM; the lectures were for the WORLD — do both. DOCUMENT: photograph every stage (the failures especially — the failure log, Step 14, needs pictures); write the one-paragraph ‘what I learned’ for each project. SHARE: maker forums, local hackerspaces, a video for the grandkids — the build multiplies when witnessed. TEACH: the Practice lesson’s oath says teach one experiment — the workshop’s version is teach one PROJECT. THE TEACHING’S CLOSE: the workshop is not about Tesla — it is about YOU becoming the kind of person who builds instead of scrolls. The tower fell; the bench remains. Twelve projects done, documented, and taught — that is the real Wardenclyffe: power generated locally, by hand, for free.

🧘 Living 3-6-9: The Embodied Practice

What 3-6-9 IS, simply — then how to instill it in your BODY: breath, rhythm, and a daily structure that runs on threes. Not numerology trivia. A way of living.

What 3-6-9 is (one minute, simply)

3 = CREATION: the triangle, the beginning, the spark — every act of starting. 6 = STRUCTURE: the hexagon, the material, the work — every act of building. 9 = COMPLETION: the everything-number, the return — every act of finishing and releasing. Begin, build, complete. That's the whole teaching. Everything below is just this rhythm, installed into a human day and a human body.

Why the BODY, not just the mind

Knowing 3-6-9 as trivia changes nothing. The teaching's claim — and the psychology agrees — is that PATTERN becomes power only when the nervous system runs it. Ritualized rhythm calms the nervous system (predictability = safety to the body), focuses attention (one rhythm instead of chaos), and compounds (small ordered acts, daily, become a transformed life). You're not memorizing numbers; you're giving your body a drumbeat.

The core practice: 3-6-9 breathing

THE technique — do this first, do this daily. Sit. INHALE for 3 counts (creation — drawing life in). HOLD for 6 counts (structure — the body working with it). EXHALE for 9 counts (completion — releasing everything). That's one round. Do 3 rounds to start; build to 9. WHY IT WORKS: the long exhale (9) activates the parasympathetic nervous system — the calm branch (see the Binary lesson). The counts give the monkey mind a job. Three minutes of this and your whole state shifts — verifiable on the first try.

Morning: the 3 (creation)

The first hour runs on 3. (1) 3 BREATHS of the 3-6-9 pattern before touching your phone. (2) 3 INTENTIONS written down — not a to-do list, intentions: 'today I create...' (3) 3 GRATITUDES spoken aloud. WHY: mornings set the nervous system's trajectory; beginning in threes tells the body 'today has order.' Tesla began his days with ritualized threes (documented) — you're running his operating system.

Midday: the 6 (structure)

The work hours run on 6. Structure your effort in blocks: 6 focused work sprints (even 6 minutes each counts at first), or organize the day's work into 6 defined pieces. Between blocks: stand, shake out, 3 breaths. WHY: 6 is the number of structure (the hexagon — nature's building shape, honeycomb). Unstructured effort dissipates; structured effort compounds. The teaching: creation without structure is just dreaming. The 6 is where dreams get built.

Evening: the 9 (completion)

The last hour runs on 9. (1) 9 slow exhales — the day's tension leaving. (2) Review in 9s: what did I complete? (name them). What do I release? (name it, let it go). (3) Write tomorrow's 3 intentions — the cycle reseeds itself. WHY: the nervous system can't rest with open loops; the 9 closes them deliberately. Sleep comes faster, deeper. 9 is completion — the day ends finished, not just stopped.

The all-day texture: threes everywhere

Once the skeleton is set, weave threes through the day: drink water in 3 pauses. Eat meals in 3 unhurried phases. When stressed: 3 breaths before responding. Speak in 3 points when it matters. Walk stairs 3 at a time in your mind. This sounds obsessive until you try it — then it feels like rhythm. Tesla's documented compulsion becomes your chosen cadence. The difference between a cage and a dance is who chose it.

The 21-day instillation

HOW IT GETS INTO THE BODY: (1) DAYS 1–7: just the breathing, 3 rounds, twice daily — learn the drumbeat. (2) DAYS 8–14: add the morning 3 and evening 9 — the day gains a frame. (3) DAYS 15–21: add the midday 6 and the all-day texture. Track it: one line in your journal nightly ('3-6-9 day X: done/missed'). WHAT CHANGES (reported consistently): calmer mornings, less scattered work, faster sleep onset, and an odd sense of order — the signature feeling practitioners describe. Miss a day? Resume. The rhythm forgives.

The honest frame

Is this 'Tesla's teaching'? The 3-6-9 pattern's cosmic claims are unverified (see the 3-6-9 lesson) — but THIS practice doesn't need them. Structured breathing calms the nervous system (established). Morning intention-setting improves follow-through (established). Evening review improves sleep (established). Ritualized rhythm reduces anxiety (established). The practice works on psychology and physiology alone — the 3-6-9 frame just makes it beautiful and memorable. That's honest embodiment: what works, worn proudly.

Step 10 — Troubleshooting: the three walls

Troubleshooting the core practice, because beginners hit the same three walls. WALL 1 — 'The 6-count hold makes me dizzy.' Fix: drop to 2-4-6 (inhale 2, hold 4, exhale 6) — the RATIO matters more than the numbers; never strain. WALL 2 — 'I lose count and get frustrated.' Fix: count on your fingers, or breathe to a slow song's phrasing — the counting is a servant, not the master. WALL 3 — 'I feel nothing.' Fix: you're likely breathing shallowly into the chest — push the belly out on the inhale first (see the Breathwork lesson), then the counts start working. If dizziness or discomfort persists, stop and breathe normally — no practice is worth forcing.

Step 11 — The 3-6-9 journal template (copy this)

A concrete template — copy this into your journal nightly. Line 1: '3 CREATED: ___, ___, ___' (three things you started or made today — even small). Line 2: '6 BUILT: ___' (one honest sentence on the day's structured work). Line 3: '9 COMPLETED / RELEASED: ___, ___' (what finished; what you're letting go of). Line 4: 'TOMORROW'S 3: ___, ___, ___' (reseeds the morning). Four lines, two minutes. WHY IT WORKS: writing closes open loops — the brain stops rehearsing what the page holds (psychologists call this the Zeigarnik effect: unfinished tasks haunt memory until captured). After 21 days, read day 1 vs. day 21 — the transformation is usually visible on the page before it's felt in the body.

Step 12 — FAQ: do the counts have to be exact?

FAQ: 'Do the counts have to be exact?' No — and insisting on exactness misses the point. What matters is the SHAPE: inhale SHORTER than the hold, exhale LONGEST. Valid versions: 2-4-6 (gentle, for beginners or small lung capacity), 3-6-9 (standard), 4-8-12 (advanced, only if comfortable). What matters is that the exhale dominates — that's what activates the calm branch of the nervous system (established physiology). Tesla's documented threes were rigid; YOUR practice should be flexible. A rigid ritual you dread is worse than a loose rhythm you keep. Adapt the numbers; keep the shape.

Step 13 — The 3-6-9 decision method

Use the pattern as a decision tool — concrete method. Facing a choice: (1) THE 3: write 3 options — not two (two options is a trap; three forces creativity). (2) THE 6: ask 6 questions — what does each option create, what does it cost, what does it require daily, who does it affect, what does my body say, what would I advise a friend? (3) THE 9: sleep on it — revisit after genuine rest, then commit fully and release the other options (the 9 is completion: decide, then stop re-deciding). WHY IT WORKS: most bad decisions come from too FEW options and too FAST a verdict — the 3-6-9 structure forces breadth then depth then closure. Try it on your next real decision and compare it to how you usually choose.

Step 14 — The minimum viable 3-6-9 (chaos days)

Travel days, sick days, chaos days — the full practice won't fit, and that's fine. The MINIMUM VIABLE 3-6-9: (1) Morning: 3 breaths before the phone. (2) Once midday: pause, 3 breaths. (3) Night: 9 slow exhales in bed. That's it — under two minutes total, and the rhythm survives. The rule: never miss twice. One missed day is life; two is a new habit forming — the wrong one. The teaching's honest note: a practice that shatters on contact with real life was never a practice, just a performance. Build the small version FIRST and the big version becomes unbreakable.

Step 15 — Ritual vs. compulsion: the honest line

The line the app must draw clearly: RITUAL vs. COMPULSION. Ritual: you CHOOSE the threes, they calm you, you can skip them without distress. Compulsion: the threes CHOOSE you — skipping causes real anxiety, the counting eats your time, the pattern spreads into everything. Tesla's documented behaviors (18 napkins, circling buildings) look, to modern eyes, like the second one — and there's no shame in that, but there's no wisdom in copying it either. Check yourself monthly: 'Am I calmer WITH the practice, or anxious WITHOUT it?' If it's the second, loosen the grip — or talk to a professional. The teaching gives you a drumbeat, not a cage. If it ever feels like a cage, put down the drum.

The 3-6-9 breath ladder (the core bodily practice, expanded)

FROM ZERO: sit tall. Breathe in 3 counts, hold 6, out 9 — that's one round. The inhale (3, creation) fills; the hold (6, structure) lets it saturate; the exhale (9, completion) empties fully. Five rounds. WHAT'S HAPPENING (honest): the long exhale stimulates the vagus nerve — established physiology, the calm-down nerve — while the counting occupies the chattering mind. The 3-6-9 is a mnemonic; the physiology is the medicine. Ten minutes of this beats an hour of anxious thinking, measurably: heart rate drops, hands warm.

Morning threes: the creation audit (practice)

Each morning, write THREE things you're creating today — not tasks, CREATIONS: a paragraph, a meal, a repaired thing, a kind act. Small counts. WHY three: it's completable — ten intentions dissolve by noon, three get done. At day's end, check them off. After 21 days, read the list backward: you'll see a body of work you didn't know you were building. The 3 isn't magic — it's the smallest number that feels like a set. Completion is a habit, and habits need small reps.

Midday sixes: the structure sweep (practice)

At midday, six minutes: scan the six load-bearing areas — body, money, space, people, work, spirit — and fix ONE small thing in the weakest one. Drink water. Move money. Clear a surface. Text someone. Close a tab. Sit still. WHY six: it forces breadth — threes go deep, sixes go wide. The teaching's claim: most chaos isn't deep problems, it's six shallow ones ignored until they braid together. Six minutes, six areas, one fix. The braid never forms.

Evening nines: the completion ritual (practice)

Before bed: name NINE things the day completed — finished, released, forgiven, or simply ended. Big and tiny both count: 'the argument ended,' 'the dishes done,' 'I stopped rehearsing the meeting.' WHY nine: it forces you past the obvious three into the overlooked completions — and the overlooked ones are where peace hides. Write them, close the book, sleep. The mind that catalogs completions stops hunting threats at 2 a.m. — give it the list and it stands down.

The 21-day installation: what actually changes (honest)

Do the full 3-6-9 day for 21 days and track three metrics: tasks completed, evenings you slept well, mornings you woke clear. The teaching predicts all three rise. WHY it would work (honest): morning intention-setting (established: implementation intentions raise follow-through), midday maintenance (prevents the chaos-braid), evening completion-listing (gratitude-adjacent, established sleep benefit). The 3-6-9 frame is the delivery system; the active ingredients are known psychology. That's not a demotion — it's the reason to trust it.

When 3-6-9 becomes a cage: the exit clause

The honest warning the other lessons imply: any pattern can become compulsion — and Tesla himself shows the shadow (the documented three-fixations). If you CAN'T skip a count without anxiety, if the ritual owns you instead of serving you, it's stopped being practice and started being OCD with better branding. The rule: the pattern serves the life, never the reverse. Miss a day deliberately once a month — if that terrifies you, talk to someone. Rhythm is medicine; rigidity is a symptom.

The 3-6-9 week: the 7-day structure

Beyond the daily rhythm — the WEEKLY architecture. THE STRUCTURE: 3 days of CREATION (the maker days — start things, brainstorm, begin), 6 days is too many — so: 3 creation days + 3 structure days + 1 completion day = 7. CREATION DAYS (e.g., Mon–Wed): new projects, first drafts, experiments — no finishing required. STRUCTURE DAYS (Thu–Sat): systems, organization, follow-through — the hexagon holding the triangle’s spark. COMPLETION DAY (Sun): the 9 — review, release, rest — close loops, forgive the week, exhale. THE HONEST FRAME: the numbers are scaffolding, not law — the value is RHYTHM (the teaching’s constant theme), not numerology. A week with a shape beats a week without one — the 3-6-9 just gives the shape a name your body already knows.

3-6-9 eating: the pattern on the plate

The pattern eats too. THE METHOD: 3 MEALS (no grazing — the teaching’s meal rhythm from the Diet lesson), 6-HOUR minimum between dinner and breakfast’s end... simpler: the 3-6-9 PLATE — 3 colors minimum per meal (the phytonutrient rainbow — ESTABLISHED nutrition), 6 chews minimum per bite to start (build toward 30 — the Diet lesson’s chewing step), 9 as the fullness signal — stop at ‘satisfied,’ not ‘full’ (the Okinawan ‘hara hachi bu’ — eat to 80% — DOCUMENTED longevity practice). THE HONEST FRAME: this is portion mindfulness wearing number clothes — and that is FINE. The pattern is a mnemonic; the medicine is attention. The plate becomes a meditation — three colors, six chews, the ninth-tenth of hunger left empty.

The 3-6-9 conversation: listening in threes

The pattern’s most transformative application — other people. THE METHOD: in any real conversation, practice the 3-6-9 of LISTENING. 3: let them speak 3 sentences before you respond — count silently; the urge to interrupt is the ego’s (see that lesson). 6: reflect back for 6 seconds — ‘what I hear you saying is...’ — the hexagon of understanding. 9: pause 9... no — pause, then respond from the 9 — completion: the response that CLOSES the loop instead of opening a new argument. THE EFFECT: people feel HEARD at a level they cannot name — the teaching’s polarity lesson would call this the feminine current (receiving) structuring the masculine (responding). THE PRACTICE: one conversation daily, the full 3-6-9 — journal what changed. The pattern that organized your breath now organizes your love.

When the pattern becomes prison: the flexibility teaching

Step 15 drew the ritual/compulsion line — here is the advanced flexibility. THE SIGNS OF PRISON: anxiety when the counts break; arranging life around threes instead of threes serving life; the pattern interrupting presence (counting breaths instead of hearing your child). THE TEACHING’S RELEASE VALVE: the ‘broken 3-6-9’ practice — deliberately do something in TWOS or FOURS once a week — proving to the nervous system that the pattern is a servant. THE DEEPER TRUTH: the masters of any pattern eventually TRANSCEND it — the musician forgets scales, the meditator drops technique. The 3-6-9 is a raft — the teaching’s oldest metaphor (the Buddha’s raft parable): use it to cross, then leave it on the shore. Clinging to the raft mid-river is how you drown.

Teaching 3-6-9: the 10-minute share

The pattern spreads by teaching — here is the 10-minute version. MINUTES 0–2: the hook — ‘Tesla was obsessed with 3, 6, and 9 — but forget Tesla; your BODY already knows the pattern.’ MINUTES 2–5: the breath — teach the 3-6-9 breathing (Step 3) right there, three rounds together. MINUTES 5–8: the day — sketch morning/midday/evening on a napkin (Steps 4–6). MINUTES 8–10: the honesty — ‘the cosmic claims are unproven; the practice works because rhythm calms nerves — try it for a week and judge by your sleep.’ THE RULES: teach the PRACTICE, not the mythology — lead with the breath, end with the honesty. The teaching spreads at the speed of usefulness — the 10-minute share is the vector. Give it away; the pattern was never yours.

🛒 Shilajit: Where to Get the Real Thing

Links to real, tested shilajit — and exactly how to vet any seller yourself. Because most people have no idea where to find the real stuff.

The golden rule (before any link)

Buy ONLY purified, third-party-tested resin with a batch-specific lab report (see the Safe-Use Guide). Every link below is to a seller known for independent testing and transparent sourcing — but VERIFY the current lab report yourself before buying. Sellers change; lab reports don't lie. These are starting points, not endorsements.

Source 1: Lotus Blooming Herbs

Consistently top-rated across 2026 reviews: single-product focus (10g gold-grade resin), Himalayan family sourcing, every batch tested by an independent US lab, no middlemen. Lotus Blooming Herbs — Authentic Shilajit. Pricier (~$60/10g) — that's the cost of real purification and testing.

Source 2: Pürblack

Ranked #1 for transparency in 2026 resin rankings: patented purification, dual-layer testing (independent contaminant screening + composition report), every jar carries a registrable serial/batch number you can verify. Pürblack — purblack.com. Premium pricing — you're paying for the paper trail.

What to check on ANY seller (the 60-second vet)

(1) Is there a CURRENT third-party lab report with actual numbers? (2) Does the batch number match your jar? (3) Is the lab independent and named? (4) Is sourcing specific (region, altitude) or vague ('Himalayan')? (5) Price reality: real purified resin costs real money — suspiciously cheap = suspicious. Run every seller through this, including the two above.

Where NOT to buy

Random Amazon/Flipkart sellers with no lab reports. Social media shops. Anything marketed 'raw and unprocessed' as a benefit. Anything with miracle-cure claims. Gas-station 'shilajit honey' sticks. If the seller can't show you the science, they're selling you a story.

The honest note on links

Links rot and companies change — if a link above dies or a seller's testing lapses, the VETTING method in step 4 is the permanent tool. Learn to read the lab report once, and you'll never need anyone's recommendation again. That's the point of this whole app: teach you to verify, not to follow.

Step 7 — FAQ: is $60 a ripoff? (the math)

FAQ: 'Is $60 for 10 grams a ripoff?' Do the math: at the trial dose of ~300mg/day, 10g lasts about 33 days — roughly $1.80/day. What that buys: hand-harvesting at altitude, traditional purification, modern filtration, and an ISO-accredited lab running ICP-MS heavy-metal panels on YOUR batch — lab testing alone costs the seller real money per batch. Compare: a daily coffee costs more. The expensive part isn't the resin — it's the PROOF. A $15 jar skips the proof, and now you know exactly what 'skipping the proof' means (see the Safe-Use Guide, Step 1). Price is the most honest ingredient list in this industry.

Step 8 — Altai mumijo: the alternative, honestly

You'll meet 'mumijo' — especially Altai mumijo from Russia/Mongolia — marketed as something distinct and often cheaper. The truth (from the Shilajit lesson): same geological family, same formation, centuries of Central Asian traditional use. The differences that matter: LESS published clinical trial data on mumijo specifically (the testosterone RCTs used Himalayan-derived extracts), and sourcing transparency varies more. The vetting rule doesn't change one bit: purified, third-party COA with heavy-metal numbers, batch match — whatever the mountain, whatever the name. A tested Altai mumijo beats an untested 'premium Himalayan' every time. Judge the paperwork, not the postcard.

Step 9 — Reading the label: the percentage game

Labels love big percentages: '50% fulvic acid!' '85% fulvic acid!' Read them carefully. (1) The percentage should refer to the TESTED resin with a lab method named — not a marketing claim. (2) Higher isn't automatically better — the clinical trials used standardized extracts, not maximum-fulvic products; there's no evidence that 85% beats 60% in humans. (3) Watch the trick where 'fulvic acid' percentage is measured on a DRIED/processed extract and the jar contains mostly filler — the COA's composition section is the truth; the front label is advertising. (4) 'Trace minerals: 85+' without a mineral breakdown is decoration. Rule: the back of the jar (and the COA) outranks the front of the jar. Always.

Step 10 — The subscription trap

The trap: a fair first jar at a fair price — then an auto-ship subscription you didn't notice, billing monthly at full price. Shilajit is a MONTHS-long tonic, so subscriptions SEEM sensible — but only on your terms. Rules: (1) Never subscribe before finishing jar one and judging results at 8+ weeks. (2) If you do subscribe, set a calendar reminder to re-evaluate every 3 months — with a re-check of the seller's CURRENT lab reports. (3) Prefer sellers who let you buy one jar with no account and no subscription nudge. A company confident in its resin doesn't need to lock you in; a company confident in its marketing does.

Step 11 — The 5-question email (copy this)

Copy, paste, send — any seller worth your money answers all five. 'Hi — before I buy: (1) Can you send the CURRENT third-party COA for the batch I'd receive? (2) Which lab performed it, and is it ISO 17025 accredited? (3) What are the exact lead, arsenic, mercury, and cadmium results and limits? (4) Where is the resin sourced (region, altitude)? (5) Is it purified — and by what method?' A good seller replies within days with documents. A bad seller replies with adjectives ('purest!', 'ancient!', 'potent!') — or doesn't reply. You now have, in one email, a test most of the industry fails. Send it proudly.

Step 12 — Re-verify yearly (sellers change)

Your vetting isn't a one-time event. Companies get bought, switch suppliers, quietly drop testing to cut costs — the supplement industry does this constantly. The routine: once a year (or whenever you reorder from a new batch), re-run the 60-second vet from Step 4 on your seller's CURRENT lab report — don't trust last year's PDF. If the reports stop appearing, the batch numbers stop matching, or the answers get vague: leave, no loyalty, no nostalgia. Your health is the asset; the seller is a vendor. The method you learned in this lesson is permanent — the sellers are temporary. That's the point of teaching verification instead of recommendations.

The grade game: 'gold,' 'premium,' 'A++'

Sellers invent tiers — 'gold grade,' 'premium reserve,' 'A++ Himalayan' — and they mean NOTHING standardized. There is no grading authority for shilajit, no official scale, no certifier of 'gold.' Each seller defines their own tiers, which means the words are adjectives, not measurements. What to do: ignore the grade word entirely and read the NUMBERS — fulvic percentage with method, heavy-metal results with limits, batch match (the Sourcing lesson's 60-second vet). Honest translation: grade words are marketing; lab numbers are the actual grades. A 'standard grade' resin with a full COA beats a 'diamond platinum gold' resin with a story, every single time.

Powder and capsules: the honest cases

Resin is the gold standard, but powder and capsules have legitimate uses — here's the honest breakdown. FINE FOR: travel (no sticky jar), taste aversion (some people truly can't do the bitterness), and precise dosing. THE EXTRA VETTING THEY NEED: (1) What's the fill weight per capsule — and is it pure resin powder or cut with fillers? The label's 'other ingredients' line tells you. (2) Is the COA for the POWDER batch, not a resin batch? Different form, different test needed. (3) Capsule shells: gelatin vs. veggie — matters to some buyers. Rule: capsules from a tested seller beat resin from an untested one — form is secondary, paperwork is primary, same as everything in this section.

Vetting an Amazon listing, step by step

Amazon is where most people actually buy — so vet it like a professional. (1) SELLER PROFILE: click the seller name — how long have they sold? A 6-month-old seller with 2,000 five-star reviews is a pattern, not a reputation. (2) REVIEW SHAPE: click 'verified purchase' filter; a flood of 5-stars in one month followed by silence is a red flag; detailed 3-star reviews are often the most honest. (3) THE QUESTION TEST: use 'Ask a question' — 'Can you post the batch-specific COA with heavy-metal numbers?' Watch what happens. (4) PHOTOS: actual COA documents in the listing images, or stock mountain photos? (5) 'Fulfilled by Amazon' means warehousing, not testing — it tells you nothing about purity. Run all five; most listings fail at step 3.

'Sun-dried and traditionally purified': enough?

Some sellers claim traditional purification ONLY — sun-drying, water settling, the old ways — as if modern labs were unnecessary. The fair version: traditional Shodhana (dissolving, settling, filtering, sometimes in herbal decoctions like triphala) is REAL and was genuinely effective for its era. The honest problem: it was designed before industrial pollution — the ancients weren't filtering for modern heavy-metal loads or verifying with ICP-MS. The app's standard: traditional purification AND modern lab verification — the methods complement each other; neither replaces the other. 'Traditionally purified' without a COA is half the equation presented as the whole.

Bulk buying: the math and the storage

Once jar one proves the seller AND your body likes it, bulk makes sense. THE MATH: a 30g jar typically costs far less per gram than 10g — at 300mg/day, 30g is ~100 days, often under a dollar a day for tested resin. WHEN: only after (1) you've finished a full small jar from that seller, (2) re-verified their CURRENT COA, and (3) run 8+ weeks with results you can feel. STORAGE for bulk: keep the big jar cool, dark, and sealed; portion a month's worth into a small jar for daily use so the main supply isn't opened daily (air and moisture are the enemies). Bulk rewards the verified — never bulk-buy from an unvetted seller, no matter the discount.

Red-flag phrasebook (decode the marketing)

Learn to read labels like a skeptic. 'WILD-HARVESTED AT 18,000 FEET' — altitude of harvest is untestable and doesn't equal quality; it's scenery, not data. 'LAB-TESTED' WITH NO LAB NAMED — tested where, by whom, to what standard? Unnamed testing is a rumor. 'AS SEEN ON [PODCAST]' — almost always a paid ad spot, not an endorsement. 'ANCIENT SECRET' — it's in published textbooks; the only secret is the COA they won't show. 'PHARMACEUTICAL GRADE' — no official standard exists for shilajit; the phrase is borrowed prestige. '100% PURE' NEXT TO NO COA — pure WHAT, exactly? The phrasebook rule: every claim should point to a document; adjectives without documents are just expensive fonts.

FAQ: no good sellers in my country?

FAQ: 'Nothing vetted ships to me — now what?' The decision tree: (1) Check whether the top sellers ship internationally — many do, and the shipping cost is worth it for a months-long supply. (2) Look for REGIONAL sellers and run the identical vetting (COA, batch match, ISO lab) — the standard doesn't change with geography. (3) NEVER downgrade your standard because of location — a bad local jar is worse than no jar; the heavy metals don't care about your shipping constraints. (4) Customs: sealed, labeled supplement jars normally clear; check your country's import rules BEFORE ordering so a good jar doesn't die in a warehouse. Geography is a logistics problem, not a standards problem — solve the logistics, keep the standards.

The 2026 market map: who’s who right now

The market moves fast — here is the current landscape (verify before buying; companies change). THE TIERS: TIER 1 (the tested specialists) — single-product or few-product companies built around shilajit, publishing batch COAs: the lesson’s Lotus Blooming Herbs and Pürblack sit here. TIER 2 (the reputable generalists) — big supplement brands with shilajit lines — decent testing, less specialization. TIER 3 (the marketplace flood) — Amazon/eBay sellers, wildly variable — some fine, many not; the COA is the only filter. TIER 4 (the scams) — no COA, miracle claims, ‘raw’ marketing. THE TEACHING’S MARKET READ: the industry is maturing — third-party testing is becoming standard BECAUSE buyers demanded it (the 2021 thallium scare helped). Reward the testers with your money; starve the rest.

Reading a COA line by line: the worked example

Step 8 (Safe-Use Guide) taught the sections — here is a line-by-line walkthrough. HEADER: lab name + ISO 17025 accreditation number — google the lab; it should exist independently. PRODUCT IDENTIFICATION: product name + BATCH/LOT number — must match your jar’s label, digit for digit. HEAVY METALS: lead (Pb), arsenic (As), mercury (Hg), cadmium (Cd) — each with a measured value AND a limit — the value must be UNDER the limit (limits follow USP/Prop 65 standards). MICROBIAL: total plate count, yeast/mold, E. coli, salmonella — ‘absent’ or under limits. FULVIC ACID %: the potency number — 60%+ for quality resin. DATE: within 12 months — old COAs are decorations. THE RED FLAGS: ‘typical values’ instead of batch values; limits without measurements; a lab that only exists on the seller’s website. A real COA reads like a blood test — numbers, ranges, dates.

The price ladder: what money buys

Shilajit pricing decoded — what each tier actually purchases. UNDER $20/10g: almost certainly fake, diluted, or untested — the economics don’t work (real purification + testing costs more). $30–50/10g: the honest middle — real resin, real testing, smaller brands. $50–80/10g: the premium tier — gold-grade sourcing, dual testing, fancy packaging — diminishing returns past ~$60 unless the COA justifies it. OVER $100/10g: luxury branding — you are buying story. THE MATH (from Step 7): at 300mg/day, 10g = ~33 days — so $45/jar = ~$1.36/day. THE TEACHING’S ECONOMICS: price is a SIGNAL, not a guarantee — a $70 jar without a COA is worse than a $35 jar with one. Buy the TEST, not the price tag — and never the story.

Bulk buying and storage: the long game

For committed users — the economics of scale. THE MATH: 30g–50g jars often price 20–30% cheaper per gram than 10g — if you have vetted the seller (never bulk-buy unvetted). SHELF LIFE: purified resin keeps 2–3 years cool, dark, sealed — it does not ‘expire’ like milk, but potency slowly declines. THE STORAGE PROTOCOL: original jar, tight lid, cool dark drawer — NOT the bathroom (humidity), NOT above the stove (heat). If it hardens: warm the closed jar in warm water 5 minutes — it softens. If it grows mold (rare, means moisture got in): discard — do not scrape and use. THE TEACHING’S RULE: buy the smallest size FIRST (verify the product agrees with you for a month), then scale up. The bulk discount is real; the commitment should be earned.

Gifting shilajit: the introduction kit

You will want to share it — do it right. THE KIT: a 10g jar of YOUR vetted brand (never gift an untested product), a printed copy of the Safe-Use Guide’s key rules (purified only, the dose, who must not take it), and your own 30-day notes (the personal testimony beats any brochure). THE CONVERSATION: ‘This is the mineral resin I take — here’s what it did for me, here’s the safety sheet, here’s where I get it. No pressure — read the safety part first.’ THE RULES: never dose someone else (their body, their decision); never gift to the contraindicated (pregnant, kids — the Guide’s exclusions apply to gifts too); never make medical claims (‘it cured my X’ — say ‘I feel steadier’). THE TEACHING’S ETHIC: share the TOOL, not the sermon — the kit respects the recipient’s sovereignty. Given well, it is the best introduction to the whole mineral teaching.

🛒 Sebi Foods & Herbs: Where to Find Everything

Where to actually find Sebi-approved foods and herbs — the official store, the markets, the staples — because most people don't know where to look.

Start here: the official store

Dr. Sebi's own company (run by his family) sells his original herbal compounds — the mineral formulas like Bromide Plus (sea moss + bladderwrack). Dr. Sebi's Cell Food — drsebis.com — this is the official site; their own verification page warns that anything not from drsebis.com isn't theirs. If you want HIS formulas, this is the source. (Note: an older official site, drsebiscellfood.com, also circulates.)

Everyday approved foods: your grocery store

Most of the Sebi list is ordinary produce: kale, cucumbers, zucchini, bell peppers, okra, onions, avocados, apples, mangoes, berries, limes, dates, figs, walnuts. Any supermarket carries these. The discipline isn't WHERE — it's choosing seeded over seedless, whole over processed. Start with what's already in your store.

The hard-to-find fruits: ethnic markets

Soursop, burro bananas, prickly pear, tamarind, Seville oranges, soft-jelly coconuts — these live in LATIN/CARIBBEAN markets and ASIAN markets, not mainstream supermarkets. Find the Latin market in your area and ask; soursop is often in the freezer section as pulp. This is also the cheapest way to eat the list — ethnic markets undercut health-food stores dramatically.

Ancient grains: health food stores + online

Fonio, kamut, spelt, teff, amaranth, wild rice — health food stores carry these (often in bulk bins, which is cheapest). Online grocers and marketplaces stock them too. TIP: buy one grain at a time and learn to cook it before stockpiling — fonio cooks in 5 minutes, teff makes incredible porridge.

Sea moss, bladderwrack, burdock root & herbs

The cleanse herbs: sea moss (raw, dried) is sold at Caribbean markets, health food stores, and the official Sebi store; bladderwrack and burdock root at herb shops and health food stores (tea/capsule/loose). For loose bulk herbs from a reputable herb supplier, look for established herb companies with transparent sourcing — and apply the same rule as shilajit: documentation over marketing. The official store's pre-made compounds skip the guesswork.

Spotting fakes (the Sebi name is abused)

Dr. Sebi's name is slapped on countless products he never touched. RED FLAGS: 'Sebi-inspired' gummies with miracle-cure claims, sellers on random social accounts, ingredients NOT on his food list, no connection to drsebis.com. His own site's rule: if it's not from drsebis.com or an authorized partner, it's not his. Same principle as everything in this app — verify the source.

Ordering online in Canada (the Canada problem, solved)

In Canada, a lot of this stuff isn't in local stores — so order it. SEA MOSS: Healing Moss (healingmoss.ca) — Canadian company, wildcrafted raw sea moss, priced in CAD, ships within Canada. DRIED HERBS (bladderwrack, burdock root and hundreds more): Golden Bough (goldenbough.ca) — Canadian botanical supplier with per-herb listings. HARD-TO-FIND ITEMS (sarsaparilla root, specific cuts): search Etsy Canada — many herb sellers ship to Canada, e.g. wild-harvested bladderwrack on Etsy Canada; always check the seller's reviews and ratings first. SEBI'S OWN FORMULAS: check international shipping at drsebis.com before ordering. RULE: dried herbs cross the border fine; order the raw materials online and make your own gels and teas — cheaper and fresher than pre-made.

The budget path

Eating the Sebi list doesn't require the official store: supermarket produce + a Latin market + bulk-bin grains + tap-to-spring water switch covers 90% of it. The compounds and sea moss are the upgrade, not the entry fee. Start where your wallet is; the list meets you there.

Step 9 — FAQ: official compounds or DIY?

FAQ: 'Do I NEED the official compounds, or can I make my own?' Honest answer: the official compounds are CONVENIENCE, not magic. Dr. Sebi's formulas combine the same herbs you can buy loose (sarsaparilla, burdock, bladderwrack, sea moss) — what you're paying for is his exact ratios, professional preparation, and quality control. DIY teas and gels from bulk herbs (see Steps 5 and 7) cost a fraction and work on the same traditional principles — but YOU become the quality control: sourcing, ratios, preparation. Beginners: start DIY with single-herb teas (one herb, learn it). Consider the compounds when you want the full traditional formulas without the learning curve. Neither path is 'more authentic' — authenticity is in the herbs, not the packaging.

Step 10 — The $50 starter shopping list

Your first Sebi shopping trip, concrete — about $50. PRODUCE ($20): kale, cucumbers, zucchini, bell peppers, avocados, limes, apples, dates. GRAINS ($10): one bag of fonio or quinoa from bulk bins. TEAS ($10): dandelion root tea and nettle tea (grocery or health store). SEA MOSS ($10–15): a small bag of raw dried sea moss (Caribbean market or online). That's a full week of eating the list, drinking the teas, and making your first gel — no official store required. The teaching's promise kept: the list meets your wallet where it is. Upgrade to compounds and exotic fruits later, or never.

Step 11 — Make sea moss gel: step by step

You bought raw sea moss — now what? Do this. (1) RINSE the dried moss thoroughly, picking out any shell bits or debris. (2) SOAK in fresh water 12–24 hours (it triples in size; change the water once). (3) RINSE again, then BLEND with fresh spring water until completely smooth — add key lime juice if you like (Sebi-approved). (4) POUR into a glass jar and refrigerate — it sets into a gel in a few hours. (5) USE within 2–3 weeks refrigerated; freeze the rest in ice-cube trays for months. Take 1–2 tablespoons daily, in smoothies or straight. That's the whole skill — twenty minutes of work for weeks of mineral gel. His followers have made it this way for decades.

Step 12 — The farmer's market advantage

Don't skip your local farmer's market. The Sebi list is built on produce, and market growers can answer the two questions a supermarket can't: 'Was this sprayed?' and 'Is this the seeded variety?' Ask directly — small growers usually know their seed sources and spray schedules. Buy what's in season (cheaper, fresher, more mineral-dense — established nutrition science: produce loses nutrients in long storage). Build a relationship with one grower and ask them to flag seeded grapes, burro bananas, or Seville oranges when they have them. The market is also where you'll find dandelion greens, purslane, and wild arugula — all on the list, often labeled as weeds elsewhere.

Step 13 — What 'wildcrafted' actually means

FROM ZERO: 'wildcrafted' means gathered from the wild (not farmed) — wild sea moss pulled from ocean rocks, wild burdock dug from fields. It SOUNDS premium, and it can be: wild plants often concentrate more minerals than farmed ones. But the word is UNREGULATED — anyone can print it, and wildcrafted says nothing about heavy metals, pollution, or correct species identification (sea moss has lookalikes). So: treat 'wildcrafted' as a nice story, not a safety claim. What actually matters — same as shilajit, same as everything in this app: who harvested it, where, and what the lab report says. Story on the front, proof on the back.

Step 14 — The 'alkaline water' trap

Common mistake: buying 'alkaline water' machines, alkaline drops, or pH powders thinking they're the Sebi teaching. They're not. Sebi's system was about MINERAL-RICH whole foods and herbs — the 'alkaline' part referred to foods that leave mineral-rich ash in the body (established nutrition concept: 'alkaline-forming foods'). Bottled alkaline water with an electrically raised pH is a different thing entirely — and some of it is just filtered tap water with baking soda. His actual water guidance was simple: natural spring water. Save the machine money; buy the sea moss. If a product needs Sebi's name plus a machine to make sense, it's not his teaching.

Step 15 — Reading supplement labels: the red flags

Flip the bottle: (1) 'Proprietary blend' with no amounts — you have no idea what you're getting; (2) magnesium stearate, titanium dioxide, artificial colors — fillers and flow agents you don't need; (3) 'natural flavors' — a legal hiding spot; (4) heavy on marketing, light on ingredient transparency. Green flags: third-party tested (NSF, USP seals), full disclosure of amounts, minimal ingredients, the actual herb name (genus + species) not just a folksy nickname. The supplement industry is barely regulated — the label is the only sheriff in town, so learn to read it like one.

Step 16 — Sea moss: pool-grown vs. wildcrafted (how to tell)

Real wildcrafted sea moss (Chondrus crispus / Gracilaria) grows on ocean rocks — thin, varied in color (gold, purple, green mixed), with visible holdfasts where it gripped the rock. Pool-grown 'sea moss' is farmed in ropes in shallow pools — thick, uniformly golden, rubbery, suspiciously perfect. The farmed stuff still has minerals, but the mineral profile of ocean-grown is richer (Associated — the ocean is the mineral source, after all). Price is the tell: if it's suspiciously cheap and perfectly uniform, it's farmed. Buy from sellers who name their harvest waters.

Step 17 — Storing herbs and foods: the shelf-life reality

Dried herbs: 1 year at peak, then they fade — light, heat, and air are the killers; store in dark glass jars, cool cupboard. Sea moss gel (homemade): 2-3 weeks refrigerated — if it smells off, it IS off. Nuts and seeds: fridge or freezer (their oils go rancid at room temp in weeks). Oils: cool, dark, and check the harvest date — 'best by' is a guess, rancid oil smells like crayons or putty. Ground flax: buy whole, grind fresh — pre-ground goes rancid fast. The rule: your apothecary is a living thing. Date everything, sniff everything, toss without mercy.

Step 18 — The bulk-buying strategy

Herbs and grains get dramatically cheaper in bulk: a pound of dried nettle or burdock costs a fraction per cup of the little jars. Split bulk bags with friends — the co-op model. Ethnic grocery stores (Caribbean, African, Indian, Latin markets) sell the same herbs Sebi used at a third of the health-food-store price — sarsaparilla, cerasee, guinea hen weed, all of it, often fresher. Online: buy from herb farms, not lifestyle brands — you're paying for the plant, not the packaging. The teaching was never meant to be a luxury hobby; the plants are cheap, the branding is expensive.

Step 19 — Grow your own: the beginner's apothecary

Four to start, nearly unkillable: DANDELION (grows as a weed — let a patch live; leaves for salads, roots for tea), NETTLE (perennial, spreads — wear gloves; spring tops are mineral bombs), MINT (grows anywhere — digestive tea on tap), CALENDULA (easy flowers — skin-healing tea and salve). A windowsill, a balcony, or a yard corner is enough. Homegrown = zero supply chain, zero doubt about sourcing, peak freshness. The teaching's deepest sourcing hack was never a store — it was dirt.

Step 20 — When 'Sebi-approved' branding lies (deeper fake-spotting)

Sebi died in 2016 — he approves nothing anymore. Red flags: (1) His face on the package — the estate doesn't license most of it; (2) 'Dr. Sebi's secret formula' — there are no secret formulas, the herbs are all public; (3) prices 5x the herb's bulk cost — you're buying the story; (4) disease-cure claims on the label — illegal and dishonest; (5) no genus/species listed — 'sarsaparilla' could be three different plants. The man taught self-reliance; buying a $60 bottle with his face on it is the opposite of the lesson.

Step 21 — The community buying trick

The cheapest way to eat this way: find your people. A buying club of 5-10 families ordering bulk grains, herbs, and sea moss splits shipping and unlocks wholesale pricing — often 40-60% below retail. Caribbean and African community stores sometimes do group orders from importers. Community gardens grow the greens for free. The teaching was communal — Sebi's own compounds came from shared herbal knowledge, not a corporation. Eat together, buy together, learn together. The lone wolf pays retail.

The official store vs. the movement: the split, explained

Dr. Sebi’s family runs the official operation — and the wider movement often disagrees with it. THE OFFICIAL SIDE: the USHA village and family company sell the original compounds — the continuity claim is real (same family, same formulas). THE MOVEMENT SIDE: independent herbalists argue the compounds are overpriced, that the herbs can be sourced and combined at home, and that Sebi himself taught self-reliance. THE HONEST ASSESSMENT: both have a point — the official products offer convenience and lineage; the DIY path offers economy and education. THE TEACHING’S GUIDANCE: start OFFICIAL for one cleanse (learn what the real formulas feel like), then go DIY if you continue (see the Herbs lesson’s preparation steps) — the official product is the reference standard, not a lifetime subscription. Lineage deserves respect; independence deserves practice.

The Latin market masterclass: shopping like you belong

Step 3 named the markets — here is how to actually shop them. THE LAYOUT: produce up front (often fresher and cheaper than supermarkets), dried herbs and spices in bulk bins or baggies along the walls, the botanica section (if present) for the medicinal herbs. WHAT TO ASK: ‘¿tienen musgo de mar?’ (sea moss), ‘¿tienen guanábana?’ (soursop) — the staff know the inventory; the language barrier is smaller than the fear. THE ETIQUETTE: go regularly, learn names, don’t haggle aggressively (margins are thin), buy the ugly produce (it’s often the best). THE TEACHING’S POINT: the Latin market is not just a store — it is the Sebi diet’s natural habitat, the food culture the list came from. Shop there and the diet stops being a ‘protocol’ and starts being a cuisine.

The Asian market masterclass: the other treasure cave

The Latin market’s counterpart — equally essential. WHAT LIVES HERE: bitter melon (Sebi-adjacent, the blood-sugar traditional), fresh herbs by the bundle (Thai basil, lemongrass, pandan), seaweeds beyond sea moss (wakame, kombu — mineral variety), tropical fruits (the soursop’s cousins), coconut products in every form. THE TEA AISLE: the great unsung section — chrysanthemum, ginger, barley teas, often pennies per bag. THE LIVE TANKS: some markets sell live fish/seafood — not Sebi-relevant (the diet is plant-based), but the freshness standard tells you about the store. THE TEACHING’S USE: between the Latin market (the Americas’ plants) and the Asian market (Asia’s plants), the entire Sebi list is coverable — the standard supermarket becomes the supplement, not the source. Two markets, one diet, no specialty store required.

Growing your own: the Sebi garden starter

The ultimate sourcing — your own soil. THE EASY WINS (grow anywhere): dandelion (it grows itself — just don’t spray), basil, oregano, thyme, sage (the approved seasonings, perennial in most zones), kale and arugula (cut-and-come-again greens). THE MEDIUM: burdock (needs deep soil — the root is the medicine), nettle (a contained patch — it spreads), chamomile (self-seeds). THE ADVANCED: soursop and tropical fruits (greenhouse or zone 10+ only). THE TEACHING’S POINT: growing collapses every sourcing problem — cost, freshness, provenance — into one practice. A 4×8 foot bed of kale, herbs, and dandelion covers a surprising share of the list. THE DEEPER POINT: the garden is the diet’s spiritual completion — the eater becomes the grower, the consumer becomes the cultivator. Sebi’s ‘natural’ finally means YOUR hands in YOUR soil.

The 6-month sourcing review: auditing your supply chain

Sources drift — audit twice a year. THE CHECKLIST: (1) Is my sea moss source still testing/sharing sourcing? (companies change). (2) Have prices crept — is the bulk bin still cheaper than the packaged? (3) Any new local options — farmers’ markets, co-ops, a new ethnic market? (4) What am I still overpaying for — the official compounds vs. DIY math, re-run. (5) What did I stop using — the shelf of abandoned experiments (every practitioner has one). THE TEACHING’S ECONOMICS: the sourcing system should get CHEAPER and EASIER over time — if it’s getting more expensive and complicated, something drifted. Simplify toward the garden, the markets, and the staples. The supply chain is part of the practice — audit it like you audit the diet.

📖 Dr. Sebi's Food Guide: Live, Raw & Dead Foods

Dr. Sebi's complete nutritional framework — his three food categories and the full approved lists, gathered from the nutritional guides his community actually uses. Everything in one place, in plain language.

The three categories (his whole system in one frame)

Sebi sorted ALL food into three tiers. LIVE FOODS: foods that are still alive when you eat them — they can keep living off the plant, they stay non-toxic when fermented, they're perishable, they contain every element your digestion needs, their pH sits near 7 like water, and they're meant to be eaten one type at a time. RAW FOODS: live foods that were preserved — dehydrated, sun-dried, lightly cooked; they keep most of their elements but start breaking down fast unless preserved. DEAD FOODS: foods with the life extracted — overcooked, over-processed, chemical-laden; they turn toxic when fermented, keep forever on a shelf, and give digestion nothing to work with. Live feeds you. Dead just fills you.

Live foods: the top tier (eat these most)

Fresh-picked herbs and greens, tree-ripened fruit, vine-ripened fruit, sprouted seeds, sprouted grains, sprouted nuts and legumes. The logic: the food is still biochemically ACTIVE — enzymes intact, minerals in living form, structure unbroken. A sprouted seed is literally growing; eating it means eating growth itself. This is the tier the whole diet is built around — as close to the plant, as recently alive, as possible.
